server-rack.definition: A metal frame or cabinet designed to hold servers and other computer equipment in organized rows.
server-rack.exampleUsage: Technicians installed the new server in the server rack.

blade-server.definition: A thin modular server designed to slide into a shared enclosure with other server modules.
blade-server.exampleUsage: The blade server shares power and cooling with other modules.

cable-tray.definition: A support system that holds and routes groups of electrical or data cables.
cable-tray.exampleUsage: Network cables run neatly along the cable tray.

raised-floor.definition: A floor built above the structural floor to create space underneath for cables, cooling air, or services.
raised-floor.exampleUsage: Cables pass beneath the raised floor in the data center.

hot-aisle.definition: A row between server racks where warm exhaust air is directed and collected.
hot-aisle.exampleUsage: Warm air leaves the servers into the hot aisle.

cold-aisle.definition: A row between server racks where cool air is supplied to equipment intakes.
cold-aisle.exampleUsage: The server fronts face the cold aisle.

ups.definition: An uninterruptible power supply providing temporary power when the main supply is interrupted.

generator.definition: A machine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.

pdu.definition: A power distribution unit that delivers and manages electrical power for multiple pieces of equipment.
pdu.exampleUsage: The rack PDU supplies power to several servers.

patch-panel.definition: A panel with many connection points used to organize and route network or communication cables.
patch-panel.exampleUsage: The technician labeled every port on the patch panel.

switch.definition: A network device connecting devices and forwarding data within a network.
switch.exampleUsage: The network switch forwarded data between connected devices.

router.definition: A network device forwarding data between different networks.

firewall.definition: Software or hardware that blocks unwanted network traffic.

load-balancer.definition: A system that distributes network requests or computing work across multiple servers.
load-balancer.exampleUsage: The load balancer sends requests to available servers.

fiber-optic.definition: Relating to thin glass or plastic fibers that carry data as pulses of light.
fiber-optic.exampleUsage: The data center uses fiber-optic links between network devices.

ethernet.definition: A type of network technology for local area networks.

bandwidth.definition: The amount of data a network connection can carry in a given time.

latency.definition: The delay between sending a request or signal and receiving the relevant response.

dns.definition: A distributed system called DNS organizes internet names in levels and translates domain names into numerical IP addresses. It also provides other information about internet resources.

vpn.definition: A VPN creates an encrypted connection through a public network, allowing people to reach a private network or communicate securely from a distance.

hard-drive.definition: A storage device that preserves digital information without power and lets computers save and retrieve files.
hard-drive.exampleUsage: The hard drive stored the server’s files.

ssd.definition: A solid-state drive stores data in flash memory chips rather than spinning magnetic disks, providing faster access, lower delay, and greater resistance to mechanical failure.

raid.definition: A storage system that combines multiple drives for speed or resilience.

nas.definition: Network-attached storage: a system providing file storage to devices over a network.

san.definition: Storage area network: a dedicated network providing access to shared storage devices.

backup.definition: An extra copy of data kept in case the original is lost.

tape-drive.definition: A device moves magnetic tape across read/write heads, allowing recorded information to be played or stored.
tape-drive.exampleUsage: The tape drive wrote the scheduled backup to compatible magnetic tape.

cloud-storage.definition: Online space used to save and access your files from different devices.
cloud-storage.exampleUsage: The team checked the access permissions for its cloud storage.

snapshot.definition: A saved copy of data or system state from a particular moment.

replication.definition: Copying data between systems so corresponding copies are maintained.

air-conditioner.definition: A system or appliance used to cool and control indoor air conditions.
air-conditioner.exampleUsage: The air conditioner removed heat from the equipment room.

chiller.definition: A machine that removes heat from a circulating liquid used for cooling.

cooling-tower.definition: An industrial cooling system lowers the temperature of hot water by letting some of it evaporate. The cooled water can then be reused to remove heat from machinery.
cooling-tower.exampleUsage: The cooling tower released heat from the site’s cooling-water system.

fan.definition: A device for creating a current of air by movement of a surface or surfaces.
fan.exampleUsage: The fan circulated air through the equipment enclosure.

vent.definition: An opening that allows air to flow for ventilation or cooling.

heat-exchanger.definition: A device passes heat from one moving fluid to another while keeping the two fluids separate.
heat-exchanger.exampleUsage: The heat exchanger transferred heat between the specified fluids without mixing them.

containment.definition: Barriers or enclosures separating hot and cold airflow around equipment.

thermostat.definition: A device that monitors temperature and controls heating or cooling.

humidity-control.definition: Systems or procedures maintaining the moisture level of indoor air.

water-cooling.definition: A cooling method that uses circulating liquid, usually water in a closed system, to remove heat from equipment.
water-cooling.exampleUsage: The facility uses water cooling for high-density computing equipment.

badge-reader.definition: An electronic device that checks an identification badge before allowing access.
badge-reader.exampleUsage: The badge reader unlocked the secure door for an authorized employee.

biometric.definition: Related to measuring distinctive physical or behavioral traits to identify or confirm a living person’s identity.

mantrap.definition: A controlled entry space between interlocking doors used to manage access to a secure area.

cctv.definition: A CCTV installation consists of cameras, recording devices, and related equipment serving a specific location.
cctv.exampleUsage: The CCTV cameras monitored the authorized areas under the site’s privacy rules.

fire-suppression.definition: The coordinated methods and equipment used to put out unwanted fires or keep them from spreading after they begin.

access-log.definition: A record showing who or what accessed a system or location and when.
access-log.exampleUsage: The security team reviewed the access log after the alert.

cage.definition: A secure enclosure separating a set of racks or equipment from other areas.

lock.definition: A device preventing a door, enclosure, or object from being opened without authorization.

guard.definition: A person responsible for protecting a site and controlling authorized access.

monitoring.definition: The act of observing something (and sometimes keeping a record of it).

technician.definition: A person who maintains and operates technical equipment during a production.

administrator.definition: A person responsible for configuring and managing computer systems or services.

dashboard.definition: A screen or interface summarizing system measurements and status.

alert.definition: A warning message about a problem or event.

uptime.definition: A period of time when something (as a machine or factory) is functioning and available for use.
uptime.exampleUsage: The service report stated uptime for the measured period and defined how it was calculated.

maintenance.definition: Work carried out to keep equipment or systems in suitable operating condition.

migration.definition: Moving data, applications, or services from one system or environment to another.

deployment.definition: Making software, equipment, or a system available in its intended environment.

redundancy.definition: Additional components or capacity intended to maintain service if another component fails.

failover.definition: The automatic or planned transfer of service to a backup system when the main system stops working.
failover.exampleUsage: The failover system kept the service running during maintenance.
